items.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I was into Prince and Michael Jackson, everything that was hot at that time.

ctx.x: My great uncle, the bass player. He was the man in the family that had all of the albums. So when he discovered I was taking acoustic bass lessons in junior high school he was so happy, he brought me over a big stack of albums to listen to. He said, “Well now that you’re playing the acoustic bass, I want you to listen to these records.” So the one record

that was in there that changed my life forever was the Massey Hall Concert with Bird and Dizzy, Bud Powell, Charles Mingus and Max Roach. And the group sound of that record. You know because I mean I was, we’re talking like 1984, so I was into Prince and Michael Jackson, everything that was hot at that time. And I still listen to that as well as checking out Bird and Miles and it was a different kind of energy. But the joy and the feeling was still there. So fortunately I was able to latch on to it you know. And…
Is it more of a physical challenge to play the acoustic bass?
